pure-announcement.rationale: This is the abstract of a peer-reviewed research paper introducing an architecture, not a product launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The corpus's nearest concepts (RAG, weak-to-strong generalization, MCP notes) build on transformer-era models but none actually covers the Transformer architecture or self-attention itself.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims cite the primary paper with reproducible WMT 2014 benchmarks and published training configurations that many groups have since replicated.

durability.rationale: The attention-only architecture this abstract introduces became the substrate of essentially every modern LLM, so the mechanism has already proven durable for nine years even though its 2017 BLEU figures are museum pieces.

actionability.rationale: The core trade-off — dropping recurrence for attention buys parallelizable training at lower cost — is the architectural decision that still determines how sequence models are built and why they scale.

atomicity.rationale: The note carries exactly one idea, that attention mechanisms alone suffice for sequence transduction, statable in a single paragraph without the paper's framing.
